newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dispute continues over vote in Mexico's Campeche.
newsitem.headline: Dispute continues over vote in Mexico's Campeche.

text.p: An opposition party on Thursday attacked the government over election results in the southern Mexican state of Campeche, saying the vote was full of irregularities.
The left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) said the July 6 election for governor was held "without legality" and that local election authorities had favoured the ruling party.

The long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its absolute majority in the lower house of Congress in the elections, as well as the mayoralty of Mexico City and two state governorships.
But it appears to have kept Campeche, an oil-producing state on the Gulf of Mexico.
PRD candidate Layda Sansores has said she was cheated of victory and organised protests in the state since the vote.
Official results from the Federal Electoral Institute, however, gave the PRI's Gonzalez Curi 48 percent of the votes, well ahead of PRD rival Sansores, who obtained 41.2 percent.
